answer: ember ties an operator’s keys to one personhood nullifier; reef places attesters in disjoint, independent branches. juniper counts identities under that nullifier: identity \(k\) needs a 3-of-5 quorum from \(2^{k-1}\) branches unused by that operator. A debut needs 3 unrelated attesters. The tenth clone needs 1,536 across 512 branches; ten need 3,069 across 1,023 branches. No member or branch can be reused for that operator, even in parallel applications, so ten heads require recruiting or bribing 3,069 outsiders.
